results.title: ACE Program Achieves World First for AI in Aerospace
results.summary: DARPA's Air Combat Evolution (ACE) program has achieved the first-ever in-air tests of AI algorithms autonomously flying an F-16 against a human-piloted F-16 in within-visual-range combat scenarios (sometimes referred to as "dogfighting").

results.title: ACE Program’s AI Agents Transition from Simulation to Live Flight
results.summary: In less than three years, artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms developed under DARPA’s Air Combat Evolution (ACE) program have progressed from controlling simulated F-16s flying aerial dogfights on computer screens to controlling an actual F-16 in flight.

results.title: DARPA, U.S. Air Force fly AI-controlled F-16
results.summary: Historic VENOM milestone demonstrates scalable AI development capabilities for the operational fleet.

results.title: ACE
results.summary: The Air Combat Evolution (ACE) program seeks to increase trust in combat autonomy by using human-machine collaborative dogfighting as its challenge problem.

results.title: Collaborative Air Combat Autonomy Program Makes Strides
results.summary: DARPA’s Air Combat Evolution (ACE) program is half way through Phase 1 and has notched several key accomplishments in anticipation of live subscale aircraft dogfights in Phase 2 later this year.

results.title: Chris Cotting
results.summary: Chris “Doc” Cotting, Ph.D., has experience as a program manager, chief engineer, flight test lead, and guidance, navigation, and control lead for multiple aerospace vehicles.

results.title: Training AI to Win a Dogfight
results.summary: As modern warfare evolves to incorporate more human-machine teaming, DARPA seeks to automate air-to-air combat, enabling reaction times at machine speeds and freeing pilots to concentrate on the larger air battle.

results.title: AIR
results.summary: The Artificial Intelligence Reinforcements (AIR) program is developing dominant, AI-driven tactical autonomy for multi-ship, beyond visual range (BVR) air combat missions.

results.title: DARPA Selects Teams to Further Advance Dogfighting Algorithms
results.summary: DARPA recently awarded contracts to five companies to develop algorithms enabling mixed teams of manned and unmanned combat aircraft to conduct aerial dogfighting autonomously.
